messages:
sam_g: heads up — ded-cluster-7 hit OOM during a long customer convo (~38k tokens). process died, kube restarted pod. saw kv_cache bytes keep climbing.
maya: ugh. any evictions occurring? logs?
sam_g: digging. eviction counters are flat. snippet:
```
kv_cache_bytes: 12,345,678,912
kv_cache_entries: 18724
kv_evict_count: 0
session_token_count: 38214
```
sam_g: this looks like fragmentation + reuse failing when sequences exceed ~30k tokens. memory not reclaiming.
eli: can you paste the perf map/profile? maybe kernel selection changed last rollout.
sam_g: uploading perf flame in thread — but quick grep shows the kernel chooser selecting non-quantized matmul for long sequences. suspecting allocation pattern change.
ops-bot: ALERT: pod/redwood-runtime-7 restarted due to OOM at 2026-11-02T14:12:15Z :boom:
maya: immediate mitigations:
- throttle incoming long sessions (reject > 30k tokens)
- enable force-evict endpoint for that cluster
- fallback to stateless generation for sessions flagged long
eli: agree. also suggest a hotfix: set KV_MAX_SESSION_BYTES=10GB on cluster 7 and enable aggressive background compaction. command:
```
kubectl set env deployment/redwood-runtime -n prod KV_MAX_SESSION_BYTES=10737418240 --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime -n prod
```
sam_g: did the hotfix. pod restarted. monitoring counters now show evict_count increasing slowly and kv bytes dropping ~1.2GB after compaction.
maya: nice. follow-up items (RFC):
1) implement defensive cap on per-session KV + clear path to degrade to no-KV when approaching cap
2) add periodic mem-defrag job (cheap compaction) for long-lived sessions
3) add a streaming signal in console when session KV > 50% cap
4) add unit tests for kernel-selection fallbacks when sequence length >> typical
eli: add a telemetry event for "kv_fragmentation_ratio" so we can alert before OOM.
sam_g: opened GH: redwood/runtime#4821 with triage notes + reproducer. scheduling postmortem with infra tomorrow.
ops-bot: CREATED incident INC-20261102-7 — follow playbook: https://redwood/incident/INC-20261102-7 :clipboard:
maya: short-term rollback option if this recurs: pin kernel selector to previous version for clusters running dedicated long-context traffic.
sam_g: thanks all. leaving monitoring on. will post updates here.
